body_markdown:
Three[dividend-paying](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/three-dividend-paying-investments-for-times-of-transition/) data center investments can rebound after a pullback that occurred after reports of technology companies financing purchases by their customers.


The three dividend-paying data center investments can rebound partly because artificial intelligence is continuing and demand for it is unlikely to subside anytime soon.


Macro economic concerns also may have factored into the dips faced by data center investments on Oct. 14 and 15. U.S. inflation accelerated in September 2026, with gas, clothes and air fares rising in price, putting a bit of extra financial pressure on consumers only weeks before the midterm elections in the United States.


Heavy investment in data centers and AI has also propelled prices up for computer chips and the consumer electronics that use them, the[Associated Press reported](https://apnews.com/article/cpi-inflation-consumer-prices-affordability-3985019a54c82421e6112fb57baba048?user_email=05aaed36cf658406cd0fbb0afb1c187c7eb6949670826643d13ce8ce528e7b0d&utm_medium=APNews_Alerts&utm_source=Sailthru_AP&utm_campaign=NewsAlert_Oct14_2026_08:46AM&utm_term=AP%20News%20Alerts) .


**Three Dividend-paying Data Center Investments Can Rebound: AMAT**


Applied Materials Inc. (NASDAQ: AMAT), a Santa Clara, California-based supplier of equipment, services and software for the manufacture of semiconductor chips used in electronics, flat panel displays for computers, smartphones, televisions and solar products, should be able to recover from a drop in its share price. Its management laid out a constructive multiyear growth opportunity driven by expanding capacity at its major customers and rising chip complexity with new leading edge and memory architectures during a meeting with analysts on Oct. 13.


The company opened a $500 million campus in Tampines, located in the East Region of Singapore, more than doubling its advanced cleanroom capacity in the country. Applied Materials’ management has reported that it already is running at volume production.


“Applied Materials is the leader in materials engineering solutions used to produce virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world,” wrote Jim Fink, chief investment strategist, in recommending a new options trade to his[Options for Income](https://www.jimfinkinvesting.com/offer/ofi-web-default-2/?source=OFIDEF01) special advisory service subscribers on Thursday, Oct. 15. Fink, who also serves as chief investment strategist for[Velocity Trader](https://www.jimfinkinvesting.com/offer/velocity-trader-web-default/?source=VTDEF01) ,[Seasonal Stock Alert](https://www.jimfinkinvesting.com/offer/seasonal-stock-alert-web-def/?source=SSADEF01) and[Jim Fink’s Inner Circle](https://www.jimfinkinvesting.com/offer/fink-inner-circle-web-default-2/?source=FICDEF01) , has traded options for more than 30 years and generated personal profits of more than $5 million.


*Jim Fink leads the[Options for Income](https://www.jimfinkinvesting.com/offer/ofi-web-default-2/?source=OFIDEF01) advisory service.*


Fiscal third-quarter financials for the period ending July 26, 2026, were “excellent,” with both earnings and revenues beating analyst estimates, Fink wrote. Income investors should appreciate the company raised its dividend in March for a ninth consecutive year, this time by a substantial 15%.


The stock’s intrinsic value is worth at least $450 per share, said Fink, compared to the midday Oct. 15 price of $427.03. For Fink’s option trade, he remarked that “bullish seasonality” is in play between Oct. 14 and November options expiration, with AMAT rising in nine of the past 10 years.


Fink not only recommends option trades, but also humorously adds he potentially has become “overeducated,” holding a bachelor’s degree from Yale University, a master’s degree from Harvard’s Kennedy School of Government, a law degree from Columbia University and an MBA from the University of Virginia’s Darden School of Business. He also is a member of the Illinois and D.C. bars.

**Three Dividend-paying Data Center Investments Can Rebound:** **Nvidia**


NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA), a multinational technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, gained additional attention with its announcement that it will co-sponsor a pluggable standard with Cisco Systems Inc. (NASDAQ: CSCO), of San Jose, California. The move was described as “positive” in a recent Citi Research note. Cisco develops, manufactures and sells hardware, software, telecommunications equipment and other high-technology services and products focused on networking, cybersecurity and AI.


NVIDIA is a current buy recommendation of *[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU)* , led by futurist George Gilder and his team of analysts. Senior Analyst Dr. Robert Castellano, PhD, is among those who talk favorably about NVIDIA’s prospects for capital appreciation.


George Gilder heads *[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU) .*


Nvidia dominates AI data center computing with its graphic processing units (GPUs), integrated systems and networking technologies, benefiting directly from hyperscaler capital expenditures, Castellano opined.


Following the launch of several personal AI agents recently, including Muse, Dots, Instinct, GrokBot and GeminiSpark, Citi Research raised its 2030 CPU target addressable market (TAM) to $300 billion. Unlike chatbots, which remain largely idle between user interactions, always-on agents like Muse can operate continuously, drive a significant increase in inference-related compute, memory and networking consumption across both enterprise and consumer workloads, Citi Research wrote.


The investment firm reiterated its “Buy” rating on NVDA with a $315 target price. A key reason is rising demand for GPUs, Citi Research wrote. NVIDIA also offers a modest forward dividend yield of 0.44%.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


**Three Dividend-paying Data Center Investments Can Rebound: DTCR**


The Global X Data Center & Digital Infrastructure ETF (NASDAQ: DTCR) is the second dividend-paying data center investment that can rebound. The fund seeks to invest in companies that operate data centers and other digital infrastructure supporting the growth of communication networks.


Its objective is to provide investment results that correspond generally to the price and yield performance, before fees and expenses, of the Solactive Data Center REITs. The fund also offers a dividend yield of 1.5%.


The fund has holdings in companies engaged in three sub-themes: data center owners, developers and operators, including data center Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs); cellular tower owners, developers and operators such as cellular tower REITs. Also included are manufacturers, designers and/or assemblers of the servers and hardware used in these facilities.


Only companies deriving at least 50% of revenue from these sub-themes are eligible, and the Index includes up to 40 such companies, providing exposure to digital infrastructure companies globally. DTCR’s three largest holdings are American Tower Corp. (NYSE: AMT), 13.72; Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR), 12.60%; and Equinix, Inc. (NASDAQ: EQIX), 12.56%.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


**Three Dividend-paying Data Center Investments Can Rebound:** **Woods’ Wisdom**


Investors wary about investing during the sometimes scary month of October for markets may be heartened to learn that events such as Black Tuesday in 1929 and Black Monday in 1987 are rare. In U.S. midterm election years such as 2026, October is historically one of the strongest months of the year, averaging close to a 3% gain on the S&P 500 since 1950.


Plus, the S&P 500 has had a big run in the past four years, with the benchmark measure of the domestic equity market up some 117.5% since then, wrote Jim Woods to subscribers of his *[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS)* investment newsletter on Monday, Oct. 12. That is a “great move higher,” but it’s not over yet, he added.


There are several reasons for optimism, continued Woods, who also heads the[TNT Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tnt-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUTNT) ,[Tactical Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tactical-trader-web-default-offer/?source=GURUTT01) ,[Five Star Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/five-star-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUFST) and[Bullseye Stock Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/bullseye-default/?source=GURUBEST1) advisory services that recommend both stocks and options. One reason is that a Bespoke Investment Group study of historical returns of the S&P 500 after a bull market’s four-year anniversary found that the median return in the following 12 months reached 16.8%, he added.


“When you’re hot, you’re hot,” continued Woods, describing the stock market’s performance by using the title of a country tune sung by Jerry Reed that reached No. 1 on the U.S. Country charts and won a Grammy Award for Best Male Country Vocal Performance.


A second reason Woods forecast stocks would climb is because earnings growth remains robust, despite surging bond yields, soaring oil prices, and a Fed that seems intent on hiking rates. Plus, the key artificial intelligence (AI) trade is staying “strong” and consumer spending remains healthy, he added.


*Jim Woods heads[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS) and[Tactical Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tactical-trader-web-default-offer/?source=GURUTT01) .*


**Three Dividend-paying Data Center Investments Can Rebound: Geopolitics**


Russia keeps intensifying its invasion in Ukraine that has included firing on buses and other civilian targets with jet-powered attack drones. Ukraine’s capital of Kyiv has been targeted directly. In response, more than a dozen automated turrets have been deployed around the Ukrainian capital as Russia steps up its use of faster drones that are more difficult for conventional air defenses to intercept. Ukraine’s Air Force indicated it is using artificial intelligence and machine vision to track targets and aim through its[Sky Sentinel system](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U5muTgzi-04) to defend against the faster Russian, jet-powered drones, creating a tactical battle in which warfare is moving towards machines fighting machines.


The war’s escalation occurred despite recent visits to both nation’s capitals by President Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who sought to broker a peace agreement. With military action taking place there, the Middle East and elsewhere, these three investments offer a potentially profitable path to receive share-price appreciation.


If investors are wary about the ups and downs of the stock market, an alternative is to trade options. An advisory service teaches how to do so.


The pure-play options service that trades into volatility to pursue quick profits is the[DayTradeSPY](https://daytradespy.com/offer/trading-room-default-editorial/?source=GURUTR1) Trading Room, advised Hugh Grossman, who is the senior leader of the the service. The[DayTradeSPY Trading Room](https://daytradespy.com/offer/trading-room-default-editorial/?source=GURUTR1) has a win rate that averages 89.8%, its[Pick of the Day](https://daytradespy.com/offer/pick-of-the-day-default/?source=GURUPOD1) service track record is 88.6%, and the[DayTradeSPY Signal](https://daytradespy.com/offer/daytradespy-signal-default/?source=DTSSIGGURU) service profits 86% of the time.


As long as there is turmoil in the world… wars, tariffs, political upheaval, you name it, “we make money,” said Grossman, who also offers[Inner Circle](https://daytradespy.com/offer/inner-circle-default/?source=GURUIC1) memberships that include all his services.


“We can’t control the events of the day, but we can take advantage of that instability by trading short-term movements,” Grossman continued. “Options on SPY provide outstanding leverage and liquidity for quick profits.”
